section.title: Git Commands — Complete Cheat Sheet
section.subtitle: Every essential Git command explained: setup, staging, committing, branching, merging, remotes and history.

topics.title: git init — Start a Repository
topics.learn: Turn a folder into a Git repository.

git.definition: git init creates a new empty Git repository in the current directory by adding a hidden .git folder that tracks all changes.
git.code:
git init
# or with a custom branch name
git init -b main

topics.title: git clone — Copy a Repository
topics.learn: Download an existing repo from a remote.

git.definition: git clone downloads a full copy of a remote repository — all files, history and branches — onto your machine.
git.code:
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
# shallow clone (faster, no history)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/user/repo.git

git.definition: git status shows which files are modified, staged, or untracked — run it constantly to know where you are.
git.code:
git status
git status -s    # short format (script-friendly)
git status -b    # include branch info

topics.title: git add — Stage Changes
topics.learn: Move changes into the staging area.

git.definition: git add copies modified/new files into the staging area (index) — the snapshot that the next commit will record. Nothing is saved to history until you commit.
git.code:
git add file.js            # one file
git add .                  # everything
git add -p                 # interactively pick hunks
git add -A                 # all changes incl. deletions

git.definition: git commit permanently stores the staged snapshot in local history with a message. Use -m for inline messages, --amend to fix the last commit.
git.code:
git commit -m "Add login feature"
git commit -am "Fix typo"      # add+commit tracked files
git commit --amend -m "Better message"  # fix last commit

topics.title: git push & git pull — Sync with Remote
topics.learn: Upload commits and download others' work.

git.definition: git push uploads your local commits to the remote (GitHub etc.). git pull fetches remote changes and merges them into your current branch.
git.code:
git push origin main           # push to remote branch
git push -u origin feature     # push + set upstream

git pull origin main           # fetch + merge
git pull --rebase              # fetch + rebase (cleaner history)

git.definition: git fetch downloads remote branches and commits into remote-tracking refs (origin/main) WITHOUT touching your working files — inspect first, merge later.
git.code:
git fetch origin
git fetch --all              # all remotes

# then see what's new:
git log HEAD..origin/main --oneline
# merge when ready: git merge origin/main

git.definition: Branches are independent lines of development. git branch lists/creates/deletes them; -d deletes only merged branches (safe), -D forces.
git.code:
git branch                    # list local branches
git branch feature-login       # create (stays on current)
git branch -d feature-login    # delete (if merged)
git branch -m old new          # rename
git branch -a                 # list local + remote

topics.title: git switch & git checkout — Change Branches
topics.learn: Move between branches or restore files.

git.definition: git switch (modern) moves you to another branch, creating it with -c if needed. git checkout is the older all-in-one command — also restores files with -- .
git.code:
git switch main
git switch -c feature        # create + switch
git switch -                    # back to previous branch

git checkout main              # older equivalent
git checkout -- file.js        # discard local changes

git.definition: git merge combines the history of another branch into your current one, creating a merge commit (or fast-forwarding if possible). Conflicts must be resolved manually.
git.code:
git switch main
git merge feature-login       # merge feature into main

# if conflicts:
#   fix files, then
git add . && git commit        # complete the merge

git merge --abort              # cancel conflicted merge

git.definition: git rebase takes your commits and replays them on top of another branch — linear, clean history vs merge commits. Never rebase shared/public branches.
git.code:
git switch feature
git rebase main               # replay feature commits on main

# interactive cleanup:
git rebase -i HEAD~3          # squash/fixup/reorder

# pull with rebase:
git pull --rebase

git.definition: git log lists commits newest-first. Powerful filters: --oneline, --graph, --author, --since, -p (patches), and searching commit messages.
git.code:
git log --oneline --graph --all
git log --author="prahlad" --since="2 weeks ago"
git log -p file.js             # show changes to a file
git log --grep="fix"         # search messages
git log -S "functionName"     # when code was added/removed

topics.title: git diff — See Changes
topics.learn: Compare working tree, staging or commits.

git.definition: git diff shows line-by-line differences: unstaged changes (default), staged (--cached), between commits, or between branches.
git.code:
git diff                    # unstaged changes
git diff --staged            # what's about to be committed
git diff HEAD~1              # last commit's changes
git diff main..feature       # branch comparison
git diff --stat              # summary only

git.definition: git stash saves uncommitted changes (tracked + optionally untracked) and reverts the working tree — useful for switching tasks without committing.
git.code:
git stash                   # stash tracked changes
git stash -u                # include untracked files
git stash list              # list stashes
git stash pop               # apply latest & remove
git stash apply stash@{1}   # apply specific stash

git stash drop              # delete a stash

git.definition: git remote links your repo to hosted copies (origin is the default name). Add, rename, inspect and remove remote URLs.
git.code:
git remote -v                # list remotes
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:user/repo.git  # switch to SSH
git remote rename origin upstream
git remote remove upstream

git.definition: Tags are immutable pointers to commits — used for version releases. Lightweight tags are just labels; annotated tags (-a) store author/date/message.
git.code:
git tag v1.0.0                       # lightweight
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release 1.0"        # annotated
git tag -l "v1.*"                     # list matching
git push origin v1.0.0                  # push a tag
git push origin --tags                  # push all tags

git.definition: git reset moves HEAD (and optionally working tree) to another commit. --soft keeps changes staged, --mixed unstages (default), --hard discards everything — destructive!
git.code:
git reset HEAD~1              # undo commit, keep changes staged
git reset --soft HEAD~1         # undo commit, keep staged
git reset HEAD~1               # undo commit, keep unstaged
git reset --hard HEAD~1        # ⚠️ discard commit AND changes

git reset file.js              # unstage a file (same as restore --staged)

topics.title: git revert — Undo Safely
topics.learn: Create a new commit that undoes another.

git.definition: git revert creates a NEW commit that reverses a previous commit's changes — safe for shared/public history (unlike reset which rewrites it).
git.code:
git revert abc1234              # undo that commit
git revert HEAD~2..HEAD         # revert a range
git revert --no-commit abc1234  # stage without committing

# prefer revert for pushed commits;
# reset only for local-only history.

topics.title: git rm — Remove Files
topics.learn: Delete files from repo and disk.

git.definition: git rm deletes a file from both the working tree AND the index (stages the deletion). --cached removes only from tracking, keeping the local file.
git.code:
git rm old-file.js             # delete + stage
git rm --cached secret.env      # stop tracking, keep file
git rm -r folder/               # remove a directory
git rm --cached -r .            # untrack everything (then add .gitignore)

topics.title: .gitignore — Exclude Files
topics.learn: Tell Git which files to never track.

git.definition: A .gitignore file lists patterns Git should ignore — node_modules, .env secrets, build output. Already-tracked files must be git rm --cached first.
git.code:
# .gitignore
node_modules/
.env
*.log
dist/
.DS_Store
__pycache__/

# stop tracking an ignored file:
git rm --cached .env
git commit -m "Stop tracking .env"

git.definition: git config stores settings at three levels: system (all users), global (~/.gitconfig, your user) and local (this repo's .git/config). Identity is required to commit.
git.code:
git config --global user.name "Sai Prahlad"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com

git config --global init.defaultBranch main
git config --global core.editor "code --wait"

# per-repo override:
git config user.name "Work Name"

git config --list   # show all settings
